Headwaters source registry - Gurugram episodic sources. Schema + design notes: docs/specs/headwaters.md (local). Build plan: docs/specs/gurugram-onboarding.md.

LICENCE POSTURE FOR THE WHOLE SCOPE: gmda.gov.in carries 'Copyright (c) 2017. Gurugram Metropolitan Development Authority All rights reserved' and states NO reuse, reproduction or redistribution policy anywhere on /terms-conditions.html or /disclaimer.html (both read verbatim 2026-08-14). That is restrictive-by-default, the same posture as DPCC in delhi.json. Consequence, and it is a design constraint rather than a footnote: every artifact built from a GMDA source in this scope is a DERIVED AGGREGATE - counts, sums, shares - never a republication of upstream rows. The tanker MIS delivery-address column in particular is not republished in any form.

DELIBERATELY NOT REGISTERED YET: the GMDA daily WTP quality reports and the HSPCB STP/CETP monitoring workbooks. Both are verified live and written up in docs/specs/gurugram-onboarding.md section 10, but neither has a repo artifact yet, and this registry rejects a watch with no lineage on purpose - an alert nothing depends on is not actionable. They land here as their artifacts do.

sources.license: restrictive, permission required: gmda.gov.in asserts 'All rights reserved' and publishes no reuse or redistribution policy - derived aggregates only, no republication of upstream rows
sources.notes:
GMDA's own bulk-water tanker booking ledger, published as a per-year XLSX at a static path that no index page links to. Verified 2026-08-14: 2019 (12,337 bookings), 2020 (9,741) and 2021 (7,208) all resolve and parse - 29,286 bookings, 1,722,822,000 litres, Rs 8.72 crore, 36 continuous months. Per booking: timestamp, dispensing station, water type, named buyer, delivery address, tanker size, amount paid, litres. No other city on the platform has tanker data at transaction resolution.

THE SERIES STOPPED AFTER 2021, and a new year appearing here is exactly the event this watch exists for.

THE SOFT-404 TRAP, and the reason detection pins expectContentType: 2022 through 2026 do not 404. They 302 to a 38,291-byte HTML error page served as 200. A status-only probe therefore reports an edition for every year it tries, forever, and reports it silently - it looks like a healthy source rather than a broken detector. Real editions answer Content-Type: application/xlsx; the error page answers text/html. That header is the only field that separates them. Support for expectContentType was added to scripts/check-upstream-editions.ts for this entry.

SECOND TRAP, for whoever next reads these numbers: absolute bookings fall 12,337 -> 7,208 across the three years, but 2020 and 2021 are COVID years in a construction-driven market, so that decline must not be published as reduced tanker dependence. What survives the confound is compositional, because it is a ratio measured inside the same disrupted period - non-potable share 29.7% -> 42.2% -> 51.2%, against tariffs stable to the decimal across all three years (potable Rs 70.5/kL, recycle Rs 30.0/kL, CETP-treated Rs 8.0/kL).

sources.license: restrictive, permission required: no licence or access-constraint statement is served with the ArcGIS REST directory, and the parent gmda.gov.in asserts 'All rights reserved' - open in the ACCESS sense, unlicensed in the REUSE sense
sources.notes:
ArcGIS Server 11.2 with a fully open, unauthenticated REST directory, 32 folders. Verified 2026-08-14: service listing, layer metadata, query with where=1=1 and outFields=*, returnCountOnly, and f=geojson returning real coordinates all work with no token. The important contrast with Surat's IGiS portal, where WFS is disabled and only rendered tiles plus attributes are available: here the vectors are downloadable.

HARVESTED TODAY (harvest_arcgis_rest.py pins a feature count per layer, so an upstream change fails the run rather than silently rewriting a layer): MCG wards 36, the NGT water-body register 824, and the GMUC drain legs.

NOT HARVESTED YET, deliberately - each lands with the surface that consumes it rather than accumulating files nothing renders: Tubewell 524, Master Water Supply Network 122, WTP Location (which publishes Chandu Budhera at 300 and Basai at 272 MLD - PRIMARY capacity figures that disagree with the widely-quoted press 400/270 and should be preferred), STP Location, Watershed_Gurugram 10, the 117 GMUC waterlogging sites, and onemap/Boundary_GMDA's MCG limit vintages 1985/1996/2008/2010/2015/2020.

TLS QUIRK: this host does not implement RFC 5746 secure renegotiation, so Python fails with UNSAFE_LEGACY_RENEGOTIATION_DISABLED while curl succeeds. The harvester sets OP_LEGACY_SERVER_CONNECT and asserts that certificate verification and hostname checking stay ON. This is NOT the same as the insecureTLS entries for cgwb.gov.in, which serves an incomplete cert chain; that flag weakens verification and this does not. Do not conflate them.

TRAP on the water-body vintages: raw layer counts are WB 1956 (ROR) 640, WB 1976 (SoI) 519, WB 2012 (WorldView) 824 - the count RISES at the end, because three survey methods have three inclusion criteria and satellite picks up construction pits a revenue record never listed. Do not publish a count comparison. What IS defensible is the per-feature in_ror_1956 / in_soi_1976 / in_worldview_2012 / in_drone / in_google_earth flags carried on the 824-row register, because that cross-attribution is GMDA's own. Even then it only describes the 2012-known population: a body that existed in 1956 and had vanished by 2012 is not a row there at all.

Second trap: Jalshakti/IOT_Water_Sensor_ggm looks like live SCADA telemetry (level, flow rate, totalizer, pressure, capacity per tank) but all 44 records carry one frozen timestamp of 16 Jan 2023 11:27-11:28. It is a single snapshot, not a feed. Verify twice before publishing that as a claim about the institution.

GMDA_Utility_Network/Utility_Network_Water_V2 is the only auth-gated service found, and nothing blocks on it since Wet_Infrastructure_caching carries the network openly. The same server also hosts FMDA (Faridabad), HARSAC, HaryanaRoads, TCP_Haryana, HSVP and Gatishakti, so the harvester is reusable well beyond this city.
